title: Created a realtime cpu animation system so characters can have realtime conversations.
author: Ok-Suspect-9855
selftext: For my games i was making it so npcs could hear and respond in realtime. I wasnt happy with how they looked so I created custom lipsync models that animate face, custom voice models for speech and tiny custom llms for the charachter brains. I will be releasing kids ones like this (the llm brains are created to be kid friendly) and photorealistic for the adult ones (will show in a follow up post). Got it working on web, pc and phones. Putting the first one on steam in a few weeks and then app store later.

comments.author: Brave-History-6502
comments.body: I don’t know why but this feels very irritating.. sorry haha

replies.author: Ok-Suspect-9855
replies.body: For this it will be an app for kids on mobile so they can talk to it or do educational content. I have adult ones as well but I keep them seperate and these one have specific models that have only kid friendly responses.

comments.author: mallcopsarebastards
comments.body: Can you explain what you mean by: the llm brains are created to be kid friendly

replies.author: Ok-Suspect-9855
replies.body: I train the llms on a custom dataset I created so they dont know about anything bad. They dont even know how to swear or say anything inappropriate becaise it is not in their training,

replies.author: mallcopsarebastards
replies.body: okay, but when you say "train" do you mean you're fine-tuning off an existing model and then restricting it's behaviour, or are you spending thousands of dollars in compute to train a conversation-capable model from scratch?

replies.author: Ok-Suspect-9855
replies.body: I do both, from scratch is not thousands of dollars its about $200 on an a5000 at Its not as hard as you think I have trained hundreds of them from scratch its easier because they are tiny models that dont need to know math and coding and all the other stuff just how to speak.
